subject: Renewal negotiation: tiered burst credits & co-term proposal
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Rios <grace.rios@novafleet.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal for NovaFleet — initial uplift + burst option

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our discussion I pulled together an initial renewal offer that tries to balance predictable unit economics with the traffic variability you've been seeing during launches. Attaching a short proposal (NF_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf). High-level summary below: 

- Base reserved units: annualize to current committed rate (no increase to baseline units)
- Uplift on committed spend: 9% (applied as an annualized price uplift across reserved compute units)
- Burst credits: 50M token credits allocated for spikes (usable for on-demand bursts)
- On-demand cap: $0.085 per 1k tokens maximum during the term (to give you cost visibility)
- Co-term: align renewal to Mar 31, 2028 (short alignment window this year)
- Billing: single annual invoice (procurement preferred flow) with quarterly usage true-up

Key questions for you: does the on-demand cap and burst-credit sizing match how NovaFleet expects to surge? Does procurement need pro-rata invoicing or is annual okay? If this looks directionally right I can loop in finance/legal and prepare a DocuSign for signature.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
David.Kim@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0123

Attachment: NF_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal summary)
From: Grace Rios <grace.rios@novafleet.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Dwyer <mark.dwyer@novafleet.com>, procure@novafleet.com
Date: 2026-10-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal for NovaFleet — initial uplift + burst option

David,

Thanks for this — looked useful. A couple quick clarifying items from procurement and finance:

- Can you show the uplift math (how 9% maps to $/unit and our average token cost)?
- Do burst credits expire quarterly or at end of term? Procurement prefers longer validity.
- We will need an explicit cap on the overage rate; $0.085 sounds reasonable but need confirmation of how it applies to different model families.
- For invoicing: procurement strongly prefers a single annual invoice that we can PO against.

Looping in Mark (CFO) and procurement so they see the thread. Can you provide a short options table (one-pager) and an editable pricing sheet for our review?

Best,
Grace
Grace Rios
Head of ML Products, NovaFleet
grace.rios@novafleet.com

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-04T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: NovaFleet renewal — need pricing flex options

Team — Grace pushed back on burst credit timing and wants the uplift math. Procurement is also explicit about a single annual invoice. Need quick options we can present to the customer today. My thinking: give them a choice of two customer-facing packages and a preferred internal concession.

Customer-facing options (numbers are illustrative):
1) Balanced (preferred)
   - Uplift: 9% on committed units
   - Burst credits: 50M tokens valid 9 months
   - On-demand cap: $0.085/1k tokens
   - Co-term: Mar 31, 2028
   - Billing: annual invoice + quarterly true-up

2) Conservative spend protection (lower uplift, longer burst life)
   - Uplift: 7% on committed units
   - Burst credits: 50M tokens valid 12 months
   - On-demand cap: $0.095/1k tokens
   - Co-term: Mar 31, 2028
   - Billing: annual invoice + quarterly true-up

Internal concession (if we need to move):
- Offer 9% uplift but allow one-time rollover of up to 25% unused burst credits for 3 months (exec approval required)

Questions for pricing/legal: margin impact on on-demand cap if we set $0.085 across all model families? We might need to granularize by model family. Attaching a short spreadsheet (pricing_options.xlsx) with line-item math.

Can you weigh in quickly? I want to send a polished one-pager + DocuSign link to Grace this afternoon.

Thanks,
David

Attachment: pricing_options.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: NovaFleet renewal — need pricing flex options

David — good framing. Recommendation for a clean customer ask: consolidate to a single recommended package to avoid decision fatigue, with a named fallback. Suggested language below for the one-pager.

Recommended offer (customer-facing) — "NovaFleet Renewal & Surge Protection"
- Uplift: 9% on committed units (straight percent applied to committed SKU rate)
- Burst credits: 50M tokens valid 9 months from effective date
- One-time rollover: 25% of unused burst credits may be rolled forward for 3 months after expiration (requires exec approval)
- On-demand cap: $0.085/1k tokens, applies to standard and family-A models; family-B/LLM-large priced +$0.01 due to higher cost 
- Co-term: align to Mar 31, 2028
- Billing: annual invoice (Net30) with quarterly true-up for usage reconciliation

Notes: 
- If procurement presses for 12-month burst validity, we can offer 12 months but increase uplift to 10% or reduce cap to $0.09 to protect margin.
- We should avoid per-model granular pricing in the first DocuSign; handle family-B as an explicit line item in the appendix.

Approve sending this as the primary ask. I will draft the one-pager language and a short DocuSign wrapper. Monica — FYI on legal/finance margin impacts.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Hi Grace / Mark / procurement,

Thanks for the quick feedback. Per your ask we've narrowed the choices and are recommending the package below as the clean path forward; I've attached the one-pager (NF_OnePager_v2.pdf) and a DocuSign link for the order form: https://www.docusign.com/ND-abcdef-2026-NF

Recommended (customer-facing):
- Uplift: 9% on committed units
- Burst credits: 50M tokens valid 9 months from effective date
- One-time rollover: 25% of unused burst credits can be rolled forward for up to 3 months (executive-signed concession)
- On-demand cap: $0.085/1k tokens (applies to standard and family-A models; family-B listed separately in appendix)
- Co-term date: Mar 31, 2028
- Billing: single annual invoice (we will accept PO + Net30), quarterly true-ups for visibility

Ask: can you confirm PO routing and whether Net30 terms are acceptable? If procurement needs Net45 we can discuss but it may affect the pricing cap. If that works I will send the DocuSign wrapper and the order form for signature today.

Thanks,
David

David — thank you. Mark has signed off on a 9% uplift assuming two changes to the proposed terms: 

1) Burst credit validity: we need burst credits to be valid for 12 months (not 9). If you're firm on 9 months we will need a commensurate reduction in the cap; otherwise 12 months is a must for our launch runway.
2) Payment terms: we need Net45 on the annual invoice (procurement notes internal approval processes).

If you can accept 12-month burst validity and Net45, we are ready to move forward. I've attached a PO stub for reference (PO_12345.pdf). Also can you provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and the model family pricing appendix for finance? Once we have an updated DocuSign I will circulate for signature.

Thanks,
Grace
